title: Unified Inference: Product Overview, PRD & Roadmap (Q2 2026)
author: Maya Patel
body:
Summary

This document consolidates the product overview, PRD-level requirements, high-level design, roadmap and themes, pricing/packaging proposals, and release notes for the Unified Inference product for Q2 2026. Unified Inference is Redwood's cross-deployment inference offering that provides a single API and operational model across Hosted API, Dedicated capacity, and Private deployments. The goal for this quarter is to stabilize the unified routing layer, deliver first-class cost controls (Redwood Optimize v2 features), and launch a refreshed enterprise pricing tier with SLA options.

Goals

- Deliver a single developer experience that guarantees consistent latency and cost predictability across deployment modes.
- Reduce unit inference cost for typical RLHF-style chat workloads by 20% through caching, batching, and quantization guidance.
- Launch pricing and packaging that supports self-serve adoption while enabling reserved capacity and enterprise SLAs for Dedicated/Private customers.
- Provide observability primitives required for customer SLAs: per-route token cost, traceable request fallbacks, and quality regression alerts.

Success Metrics (KR-oriented)

1. Reduce median token cost for customers in the 90th percentile workload profile by 20% vs Q1 baseline.
2. Achieve 99.9% regional availability for Hosted requests in production (SLO measured across regions).
3. Convert 8% of high-usage self-serve orgs to reserved Dedicated contracts within 90 days of availability.
4. Surface cost/quality regression alerts for >= 90% of model rollouts with automatic guardrail suggestions.

Scope

In-scope:
- Unified routing layer improvements (policy engine, fallback rules, model variant catalog).
- Redwood Optimize v2: batching, prefix/KV cache improvements, quantization recommendations UI.
- Pricing & packaging: new "Enterprise Dedicated" SKU, burst/commit options, billing metrics.
- Console: per-route dashboards, trace links, and rollout controls (canary/A-B).

Out-of-scope (this quarter):
- Major runtime kernel re-architect (kernel-level perf work continues under eng-serving-runtime but not part of this PRD).
- Support for experimental model architectures (edge-specialized models) beyond curated catalog.

Requirements

Functional Requirements

1. API parity: The top-level REST/SDK surface must accept the same request schema for Hosted, Dedicated, and Private deployments.
   - Example endpoint: POST /v1/unified/generate
   - Request fields: model, deployment_hint (hosted|dedicated|private), prompt, streaming (bool), functions (optional)
2. Routing policies: Admins must be able to create routing policies by tag (latency-sensitive, cost-sensitive, region, customer-tier) with priority and fallback chains.
   - UI: policy editor in Console with validation for incompatible model variants.
3. Redwood Optimize v2 must provide automated batching profiles and KV cache suggestions per route. Recommendations must include estimated cost delta and latency impact.
4. Pricing & billing: Each request must be annotated with billing tags that allow per-route/per-model cost attribution and reserved capacity amortization.
5. Observability: Console must show per-route latency P50/P95/P99, token counts, per-token cost, error rate, and last model rollout.

Non-functional Requirements

- Latency: For latency-sensitive policies, cold-start p50 <= 80ms and streaming first-byte <= 250ms for base 1k tokens on Dedicated pools.
- Scalability: System must support 2x current peak QPS with no degradation in P95 latency for dedicated customers.
- Security: All Private deployments must support KMS integrations and have audit logging enabled for model selections and routing policy edits.
- Reliability: SLO for Hosted API regional availability = 99.9% per month. Error budget policy follows eng-sre standards.

Design & Architecture (high-level)

1. Control Plane (Console + API):
   - Policy Service: persists routing policies, validates model compatibility, exposes evaluation API for the router.
   - Billing Annotator: middleware that tags requests with billing metadata (route_id, model_variant_id, commit_id).

2. Data Plane (Serving Runtime):
   - Router: consults local cache of policies to select target deployment; supports fallback chain.
   - Adapter: translates unified request to deployment-specific call (hosted endpoint, dedicated pool call, or private gateway).
   - Cache Layer: shared KV/prefix cache service with per-customer isolation and TTLs.

3. Observability & Telemetry:
   - Token-level traces emitted from runtime to tracing pipeline; sampled for heavy flows.
   - Per-route metrics exported to metrics DB with dashboards in Console.

Sequence Diagram (textual)

1. Client -> Unified API: POST /v1/unified/generate {model, deployment_hint, prompt}
2. Control Plane -> Billing Annotator: attach tags (route_id, customer_tier)
3. Router consults Policy Service local cache and selects target deployment
4. Adapter forwards request to Serving Runtime; Cache Layer consulted for prefix responses
5. Runtime emits metrics/traces; response returns to client with billing headers

Configuration & Example (table)

| Setting | Description | Example |
|---|---:|---|
| routing.policy.priority | Integer priority for policy matching | 10 |
| routing.policy.fallbacks | Ordered list of model_variant_ids used when primary unavailable | gptx-32q, gptx-16q, gptx-8q |
| optimize.batch.target_latency_ms | Target latency for batching algorithm | 150 |
| billing.commit_id | Reserved capacity commit identifier (for amortization) | commit-2026-q2-42 |

API Example (curl)

curl -X POST https://api.redwood.ai/v1/unified/generate \
  -H 'Authorization: Bearer $KEY' \
  -d '{"model":"gptx-32q","deployment_hint":"dedicated","prompt":"Summarize the following...","streaming":true}'

Roadmap & Themes (Q2\u2013Q3 2026)

Themes:
- Developer-first predictability: API parity + clear billing attribution.
- Cost-aware serving: automate batching/caching/quantization suggestions.
- Enterprise readiness: Dedicated SLAs, billing commits, KMS support for Private.

Milestones:
- 2026-04-15: Policy Service v1 deployed (local cache + UI editor beta).
- 2026-05-20: Redwood Optimize v2 internal alpha (batching engine + UI recommendations).
- 2026-06-01: Pricing & packaging launch: Enterprise Dedicated SKU + self-serve burst options.
- 2026-07-15: Console per-route dashboards GA + rollout controls (canary/A-B).
- 2026-09-01: Private deployment KMS/HSM integration and audit logging GA.

Pricing & Packaging Notes

Principles:
- Keep entry friction low with self-serve Hosted pricing.
- Surface clear cost levers (batching, cache, quantization) that customers can act on.
- Provide committed Reserved Capacity for Dedicated with monthly/annual options and a burst buffer.

Proposed SKUs (summary table):

| SKU | Target customer | Billing model | Key differentiator |
|---|---|---:|---|
| Hosted (standard) | PLG/self-serve devs | per-token + per-embedding | Instant onboarding, pay-as-you-go |
| Dedicated (commit) | Scale customers | monthly commit (vCPU/GPU units) + per-token overage | Predictable throughput, SLA-backed latency |
| Enterprise Dedicated | Regulated/enterprise | annual commit + premium support | SLA, KMS/HSM, dedicated audit logs |
| Private (VPC/on-prem) | Highly regulated | license + infra + support | Customer-managed networking, air-gapped option |

Example pricing bands (illustrative):
- Dedicated monthly commit: starting $15k/month for 1 T4-like capacity equivalent; volume discounts at 3x and 10x.
- Enterprise Dedicated: custom pricing; typical deals start at $75k/year with SLA credits.

Billing & Metering changes required:
- Add per-route billing tags in request path.
- Emit commit_id for reserved capacity allocation to billing pipeline.
- Update invoicing templates to show amortized Dedicated costs and burst charges.

Release Notes (v2.0.0 \u2014 2026-06-01)

Highlights:
- Unified API: unified/generate endpoint (GA) with deployment_hint and billing annotations.
- Policy Service v1: create/edit routing policies and preview evaluation on sample requests.
- Redwood Optimize v2 (alpha): first-generation batching and KV cache suggestions in Console.
- Pricing & packaging: Enterprise Dedicated SKU announced; self-serve burst options live for Hosted.

Notable fixes and improvements:
- Fixed rare router cache invalidation that caused transient model-mismatch errors (eng-serving-runtime).
- Improved billing latency attribution for multi-model rollouts.
- Console: per-route metrics panel added with drill-down traces.

Rollout Plan

1. Canary (internal): 2% traffic routed through policy v1; verify metrics and billing tags. Duration: 1 week.
2. Beta (selected customers): invite 10 existing Dedicated customers to test Enterprise Dedicated pricing and KMS flows. Duration: 4 weeks.
3. General availability: open to all customers with migration docs, SDK updates, and pricing page updates.

Operational Runbooks (high-level)

- Incident triage: If policy evaluation latency > 200ms P95, route to fallback path and page oncall SRE.
- Billing mismatch: if invoicing shows unexpected amortization, re-run billing annotator logs for commit_id reconciliation.
- Rollback: Console includes a rollback button that reverts to previous policy version and invalidates local caches.

Dependencies

- eng-serving-runtime: cache and adapter stability work (kernel perf improvements out-of-band).
- eng-sre: SLO acceptance testing for 99.9% region availability.
- finance-and-legal: finalize Enterprise contract templates and invoicing changes.
- security-and-compliance: KMS/HSM approval and auditing requirements for Private.

Risks & Mitigations

- Risk: Routing policy bugs could route high-volume traffic to expensive model variants.
  Mitigation: Add dry-run policy evaluation, budget guardrails, and automatic throttling for cost thresholds.
- Risk: Billing mismatch between commit amortization and usage.
  Mitigation: Early billing pipeline audits with finance and synthetic traffic tests.
- Risk: Customers misconfigure caching leading to stale responses.
  Mitigation: Default conservative TTLs, clear UI warnings, and cache invalidation APIs.

Open Questions

1. What is the default fallback chain for cross-region failures? (regional first, then cost-tier)
2. Should the Console expose suggested quantization profiles as one-click actions or recommendations only?
3. How granular should per-route billing be (route-level vs route+model variant)?

Appendix: Migration checklist for customers

1. Review routing policies and tag existing routes for priority.
2. Opt-in to Redwood Optimize v2 recommendations in Console (beta).
3. For Dedicated customers with commits: provide commit_id to accounts team for amortization.
4. Schedule private deployment upgrade window with eng-private-deployments if using KMS/HSM.
